## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's cli-flags rule requires an environment default for every newly added flag and CI sets options that way. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic or the added tests, which were read and not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to the archive CLI; `collect()` skips files whose basename matches any pattern and logs each skip. It also adds a row to `docs/flags.md`, five tests, and one fixture file, `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` argument, `args.exclude` is `[]` and `.log` files are archived, because the flag is declared with a hard-coded `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable (for `--dry-run`, `ARCHIVE_DRY_RUN`), because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that configure the tool through the environment cannot exclude files, so archives silently contain files meant to be skipped. — Fix: Define how one `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` value splits into several globs, since the flag is repeatable, then document the variable in `docs/flags.md` and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
